newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open flat, seen trading in range.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open flat, seen trading in range.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened unchanged on Monday and were expected to trade in a narrow range as the closing of the U.S. market for Memorial Day kept many investors on the sidelines, dealers said.
"It is unchanged. The market is not going to move at all today. It will be shut down by noon," said one T-bill trader with one bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill traded with a yield 2.97 percent, unchanged from the close of trading on Friday.

While there is no official close planned for the Canadian money market, dealers said activity is expected to trail off with the U.S. market closed for Memorial Day and London observing a banking holiday.
Looking ahead, dealers said the focus for the week will be new supply in both Canadian and U.S. bond markets, which could put downward pressure on fixed-income markets.
"Considering that we're at expensive levels in recent ranges, I'm not that enthused with the market. I think a better buying opportunity will present itself later this week," the trader said.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill traded unchanged to yield 3.35 percent. The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 3.70 percent from 3.71 percent.
The call loan rate traded at 3.0 percent, the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
